Updated 16 October 2026 from the owner’s as-built report. Two Pass BIAMP 6-24 boards have been assembled and installed in the crossover chassis. Each board implements one loudspeaker channel with three signal outputs. Both boards follow the same architecture. This status confirms the reported physical implementation only; it does not establish electrical commissioning, measured DC compatibility or acoustic validation.

Electrical caution: The R LOW T4 pad is not electrically verified until copper-net continuity is measured on the assembled board. The schematic and layout establish the intended functional mapping, not the actual board net.

Electrical validation gates before amplifier/driver connection

  1. With power off, measure continuity from the L HIGH takeoff to the intended R LOW T4-side injection node and onward to the first 10 kΩ resistor node.
  2. Verify the omitted R LOW input-buffer circuitry cannot drive, load or otherwise interfere with the injection node.
  3. Measure DC at both sides of the handoff relative to supply return and the internal reference (VREF).
  4. Verify retained R LOW filter-stage bias conditions and VREF/signal-return continuity.
  5. Measure the MID electrical response and loading across the intended ≈300 Hz–1.9 kHz band.
  6. Confirm that the 50 kΩ attenuator changes MID only and does not change LOW or HIGH.
  7. Into representative amplifier input loads, verify LOW/MID/HIGH output DC, gain, headroom and frequency response.
  8. Compare corresponding rails, bias, output levels and responses on both assembled boards.

Driver protection: During commissioning, do not connect or expose CD44-PK compression drivers to an unverified full-range or misrouted signal. Validate routing and output response into safe representative loads first.

Frequency controls and candidate settings

Each standard Nelson Pass frequency control uses 10 kΩ fixed in series with an independent 50 kΩ trimmer, giving 10–60 kΩ effective resistance. Two cascaded 12 dB/octave stages provide four independently adjusted elements per branch for 24 dB/octave. These frequency trimmers are distinct from the dedicated MID level attenuator. [S1; S6]

Branch / PassXO elementEffective R (fixed + trim)Physical trim resistance (effective R − 10 kΩ)Proposed capacitor
L HIGH HP / R115 kΩ5 kΩC1: 22 nF
L HIGH HP / R251 kΩ41 kΩC2: 22 nF
L HIGH HP / R336 kΩ26 kΩC3: 22 nF
L HIGH HP / R434.8 kΩ24.8 kΩC4: 22 nF
L LOW LP / R542 kΩ32 kΩC5: 22 nF
L LOW LP / R642 kΩ32 kΩC6: 11 nF = 10 nF + 1 nF in parallel
L LOW LP / R742 kΩ32 kΩC7: 22 nF
L LOW LP / R842 kΩ32 kΩC8: 11 nF = 10 nF + 1 nF in parallel

R1–R8 and C1–C8 here are PassXO simulation labels; they do not establish unique physical PCB reference designators. The trim numbers are resistance targets, not rotation percentages. All are within the standard control range. The 10 nF + 1 nF parallel pairs are proposed population for C6 and C8, not confirmed soldered parts.

Simulation evidence and limits

The supplied PassXO screenshot shows both branches in cascaded mode, the values above and the high-pass phase-invert checkbox unchecked. The candidate uses 24 dB/octave per branch. The displayed curves suggest a nominal intersection approximately 250 Hz at around −6 dB each, with a nearly flat ideal electrical sum. These are screenshot-derived estimates, not cursor readings, exported numerical results, a fresh simulation run or measured hardware. No exact crossover frequency, ripple specification or acoustic summation is established.

A narrower 10 kΩ / 25 kΩ trimmer arrangement remains a future consideration only: it is neither selected nor implemented. The present candidate uses the standard 10 kΩ fixed + 50 kΩ trim controls; do not reinterpret the settings above for a different control arrangement.

01 / Preserved 300 Hz baseline architecture

LOW≈300 Hz LPL LOW → bass amplifier
MID≈300–1900 HzL HIGH → R LOW → mid amplifier
HIGH≈1.9 kHz HPR HIGH → high-frequency amplifier

Use two boards for stereo: one handles all three bands of the left loudspeaker, the other all three bands of the right loudspeaker. “L” and “R” below identify sections on one board; they no longer identify left and right loudspeakers.

The MID transfer is the product of two filters: Hmid(f) = Hhigh-pass,300(f) × Hlow-pass,1900(f). Neither filter alone produces the mid band. Feeding the entire stock R section from L HIGH would also high-pass the HIGH output at 300 Hz; that differs from the explicitly requested independent R HIGH path.

The approximate 300 Hz and 1.9 kHz values are the owner-confirmed as-built architecture targets. Final electrical/acoustic responses, slope, capacitor population and polarity remain measurement questions. The L HIGH → R LOW jumper is physically owner-confirmed at the T4-side BIAS resistor pad; copper-net continuity is still pending.

02 / Schematic-verified modification map

The inspected schematic has separate LOW and HIGH input attenuators and buffers. The L HIGH input can therefore keep its dedicated 50 kΩ control and buffer while feeding the MID chain. The final HIGH filter output node is before the positive terminal of its 10 µF output capacitor. Beyond that capacitor are the 100 Ω series resistor and the 47 kΩ output-to-return resistor. [S1, p. 4]

Revision 3 as-built: the owner confirms that the 10 µF output coupling capacitor, 100 Ω series output resistor (100R, not 100 kΩ) and 47 kΩ output-to-return resistor are omitted. Retain both required filter stages, their active buffers and matched bias parts. The internal signal must be taken upstream of the omitted capacitor; the now-disconnected external HIGH output pad is not an equivalent takeoff.

03 / The 50 kΩ level trimmer

Before L HIGH only

Owner confirms the dedicated 50 kΩ level trimmer is placed in the MID branch before L HIGH. It must not attenuate the input feeding L LOW or the independent input feeding R HIGH. Its action therefore carries through both MID filters and changes the final MID level.

At the functional level, a potentiometer used as an attenuator has its top connected to the branch signal, bottom to the appropriate signal return, and wiper to the destination input. Confirm the actual board’s input coupling and reference before assigning those terminals to pads.

A raw potentiometer wiper is not a constant low-impedance source. For an unloaded 50 kΩ pot driven from negligible impedance, its maximum Thevenin resistance is 12.5 kΩ at half rotation: Rsource = Rtop ∥ Rbottom. Loading changes the attenuation law. Keep or provide the required input buffering if the filter otherwise sees this varying resistance; do not assume a direct wiper-to-RC connection preserves the tuning.

This is the owner-confirmed as-built placement; verify on the assembled board that the control changes MID alone. Trace any common feed and separate it where required. Verify that turning this control changes MID alone at all three output connectors.

04 / Kit devices, supply and bias

Verified reference notes

The official 6-24 article describes level controls and input buffers, selectable 6/12/18/24 dB/octave filtering, and individually selected JFET/bias-resistor pairs. Its supply is nominally 24 V DC with passive RC filtering and a midpoint virtual reference. Buffer current is approximately 8 mA. It discourages exceeding 30 V and requires capacitor-rating checks above 24 V. A source inconsistency matters: the BOM lists J114, while customization notes specify J113. Confirm actual kit contents. Frequency controls turn upward clockwise; electrical settings do not guarantee acoustic summation. [S1, printed PDF pp. 4–7, 10–11]

The public DIY FE 2022 article describes a separate discrete gain stage with a differential input, a bipolar gain stage and JFET current sources. It discusses alternate devices, supply arrangements and gain configurations. Those options do not specify this crossover’s wiring or supply. [S2, pp. 1–3]

What this build keeps

User reported The kit devices were identified in the discussion as JCJ113N21, J113-family N-channel JFETs. This marking was reported in the recovered conversation; no package photograph was available for independent reading. The user explicitly stated that the supplied devices are matched to their resistors and decided against replacing them.

Keep each device with its supplied bias resistor and identifying label. Do not mix pairs while sorting or populating the boards. If a pair’s identity is lost, recover its selection data or re-characterize it rather than assigning a resistor by appearance.

Substitution discussion

The user raised 2SK209 and U310 only as a possible future experiment, not as approved build changes. Neither is established here as a drop-in replacement. Replacing a JFET requires verification of package pinout, ratings and operating point; matching current alone does not establish identical circuit behavior.

The previous assistant predicted little audible difference from a correctly biased substitution. That prediction was not backed by a listening result for this build. The user correctly noted that measured differences do not necessarily become audible differences. If an experiment is pursued separately, control gain, level, load and bias, then assess both behavior and listening. No sonic superiority is claimed in this dossier.

Power and DC checks

Distinguish the DC supply return, internal virtual reference, signal return and chassis connection on the actual schematic. They are not interchangeable merely because each is described as “ground.” Before any internal handoff, measure the DC level on both sides using the intended reference.

The supply current required by a modified stereo build is not established here. It must be determined from populated circuitry and verified under load. Do not copy a transformer, supply-voltage choice or bias value from the separate FE project into the 6-24.

05 / Assembly rationale and order

For the recorded design rationale, draw and label one complete speaker channel first, then duplicate it. Mark L/R section names on the drawing and LOW/MID/HIGH on the external connectors. This prevents a stock stereo naming convention from becoming a wiring error.

  1. Preserve the as-built map. Record physical board identifiers, retained filter stages, T4-side handoff, omitted parts, independent R HIGH feed and MID trim. Add the missing assembly photographs/annotation if available; measure copper continuity before powered validation.
  2. Preserve selection information. Sort passive parts without separating JFET/resistor pairs. Record orientation and pair identity before soldering.
  3. Populate accessible parts first. Fit low-profile parts before taller parts where practical. Inspect values, joints, polarity and pinout before adding parts that obstruct access.
  4. Verify power before audio connections. Check resistance for obvious shorts, apply an appropriately current-limited supply and record supply and reference voltages. Compare corresponding stages across boards.
  5. Test the filters and handoff. Use low-level signals into representative amplifier input loads. Check all three outputs and the combined MID response, then verify the second board matches.
  6. Connect amplifiers and drivers progressively. Establish safe gains and outputs before exposing a high-frequency driver to the system. Label every cable.

Use short, mechanically secured internal signal wiring and plan signal returns deliberately. Keep supply wiring and switching-noise sources away from sensitive signal wiring. The final grounding arrangement must be checked for hum in the assembled system.

06 / Alignment, measurements and listening

REW source missing

REW Gain Alignment.txt was not available. No microphone distance, reference level, amplifier gain, trim position, timing reference or saved measurement from that file is claimed below. This is a proposed commissioning procedure, not a transcription of the missing document.

  1. Measure electrical LOW, MID and HIGH responses with the intended loads. Record the signal level, controls, jumpers, supply voltage and test load.
  2. Confirm that the MID trim changes MID alone. Recheck the MID response at several trim settings to detect loading-related changes.
  3. Measure individual drivers with consistent microphone position and measurement reference. Set branch levels conservatively.
  4. Inspect adjacent-driver summation near each crossover. Explore polarity and physical/time alignment based on measured acoustic behavior; do not assign final polarity from filter names alone.
  5. Check the complete loudspeaker response and useful listening positions. Compare the two speaker channels.
  6. Listen at controlled levels, record changes and repeat measurements when settings change. Retain a known baseline so experiments are reversible.

The owner-confirmed 300 Hz and 1.9 kHz values are approximate architecture targets, not measurements of electrical or acoustic response and not proof of safe driver excursion. A MID path also accumulates phase from both of its filters. Review each transition in the actual three-way system.

Warnings that affect this build

  • A full-range signal on the wrong output can damage a high-frequency driver. Verify routing before connecting it.
  • Do not connect an internal DC-biased node directly to an amplifier input without checking its coupling and offset requirements.
  • Omitting a shared input stage may affect both R branches unless their feeds are deliberately separated.
  • Incorrect pinout or a mismatched bias resistor can invalidate an otherwise correct assembly.
  • Changing slopes, capacitor values or bypass links requires renewed response and headroom checks.

07 / Concise build checklist

  • Two boards owner-confirmed assembled and installed; physical photographs and dated board identifiers are not present in the supplied HTML.
  • Measure power-off continuity of the L HIGH → R LOW T4-side handoff on each board.
  • Verify supply/reference, filter bias and output DC before amplifier or driver connection.
  • Measure LOW, MID and HIGH gain, headroom and frequency response into representative amplifier input loads.
  • Verify MID ≈300 Hz–1.9 kHz response and confirm the 50 kΩ trim affects MID only.
  • Verify independent R HIGH input and ≈1.9 kHz HP routing before any CD44-PK driver is connected.
  • Preserve required filter buffers, coupling, DC references and final output drive.
  • Keep every supplied JFET with its selected bias resistor; verify pinout.
  • Record capacitor values, selected slopes and jumper positions for both boards.
  • Check supply, reference, bias, output DC and headroom before drivers.
  • Verify the three electrical responses, isolated MID trim action and stereo matching.
  • Align acoustic levels, polarity and summation; save settings and measurements.
